questions.question: A boatman rows 15 km in 15 minutes, along the stream and 10 km in 1 hour against the stream. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed (u) = (15 km ÷ 15) × 60 = 60 km/hr.

Upstream speed (v) = 10 km ÷ 1 = 10 km/hr.

**Speed of boat** in **still water** = (u + v) ÷ 2 = (60 + 10) ÷ 2 = 35 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 35 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Downstream Distance = 15 km, Downstream Time = 15 min = 15/60 hr = 1/4 hr.

Upstream Distance = 10 km, Upstream Time = 1 hr.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of boat (B) = (Downstream speed + Upstream speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/227b76e3c5beff960c54fb9259b74b1cc8eefae96330289c2586feb72b45ff6f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Downstream Speed (u) = 15 ÷ (1/4) = 15 × 4 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Upstream Speed (v) = 10 ÷ 1 = 10 km/hr

⇒ Speed of boat in **still water** = (60 + 10) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of boat = 70 ÷ 2 = 35 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 35 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

The speed of the stream or current (w) is calculated as half the difference between downstream and upstream speeds: w = (u − v) ÷ 2.

Downstream vs Upstream

Downstream speed (u) = Boat speed (B) + Stream speed (w). Upstream speed (v) = Boat speed (B) − Stream speed (w).

Time Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. For example, 15 min = 15/60 = 0.25 hours.</p

questions.question:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be correct? 

5 and 4

I. 4 + 8 × 5 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

II. 5 × 3 - 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1a2f9ab33e780cba5010b6de702b28619de1d1b1c922808fce2123379d05d37.png] 

I. Given equation : 4 + 8 × 5 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

After interchanging the given two numbers 5 and 4 the equation is as follows : 5 + 8 × 4 - 7 ÷ 1 = 30

⇒ 5 + 8 × 4 - __**7 ÷ 1**__ = 30

⇒ 5 + __**8 × 4**__ - 7 = 30

⇒ __**5 + 32**__ - 7 = 30

⇒ __**37 - 7**__ = 30

⇒ **30 = 30**

**LHS = RHS**

II. Given equation : 5 × 3 - 4 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11

After interchanging the given two numbers 5 and 4 the equation is as follows : 4 × 3 - 5 + 6 ÷ 2 = 11

⇒ 4 × 3 - 5 + __**6 ÷ 2**__ = 11

⇒ __**4 × 3**__ - 5 + 3 = 11

⇒ __**12**__ - 5 __**+ 3**__ = 11

⇒ __**15 - 5**__ = 11

⇒ 10 ≠ 11

LHS ≠ RHS

∴ Here, only equation I is true.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only I".**

⇒ 9 + 18 - __**3 × 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**9 + 18**__ - 6 = 18

⇒ __**27 - 6 **__= 18

⇒ 21 ≠ 18

**Option 2****):**** × and +**

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 × 3 + 2 = 18

⇒ __**27 ÷ 3**__ - 18 × 3 + 2 = 18

⇒ 9 - __**18 × 3**__ + 2 = 18

⇒ __**9**__ - 54 __**+ 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**11 **____**- 54**__ = 18

⇒ - 43 ≠ 18

**Option 3****):**** + and ÷ **

Given equation is: 27 ÷ 3 - 18 + 3 × 2 = 18

After inserting the mathematical operators in given equation the equation is as follows: 27 + 3 - 18 ÷ 3 × 2 = 18

⇒ 27 + 3 - __**18 ÷ 3**__ × 2 = 18

⇒ 27 + 3 - __**6 × 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**27 + 3**__ - 12 = 18

⇒ __**30 - 12**__ = 18

⇒ **18 = 18**

**LHS = RHS**

**Option 4****):**** ÷ and × **

⇒ 27 × 3 - 18 + __**3 ÷ 2**__ = 18

⇒ __**27 × 3**__ - 18 + 1.5 = 18

⇒ __**81**__ - 18 __**+ 1.5**__ = 18

questions.question: Which among the following is the coldest planet in the solar system?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Uranus.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranus:**

 
 
• Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun and has the coldest atmosphere in the Solar System.
 
• Its minimal temperature can drop as low as -224 degrees Celsius (-371 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• The extreme cold is due to a combination of its distance from the Sun and its peculiar axial tilt, which causes extreme seasonal variations.
 
• Unlike other gas giants, Uranus has a lower internal heat output, contributing further to its cold temperatures.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Mars:**

 
 
• Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and has a very thin atmosphere, leading to cold temperatures, but not nearly as cold as Uranus.
 
• Average temperatures on Mars range from -125°C (-195°F) at the poles in winter to 20°C (68°F) in the day during summer at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Neptune:**
 
 
• Neptune, the eighth planet from the Sun, is also extremely cold, but slightly warmer than Uranus due to its greater internal heat.
 
• Neptune's atmospheric temperatures can drop to around -214 degrees Celsius (-353 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
 
 
• **Saturn:**
 
 
• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and, while cold, it is warmer than Uranus and Neptune.
 
• Temperatures in Saturn's upper atmosphere are around -178 degrees Celsius (-288 degrees Fahrenheit).

questions.question: Banks are required to keep some reserves in liquid form with themselves. This is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Statutory liquidity ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statutory liquidity ratio (SLR)** is a **monetary policy tool **used by the **central bank of a country** to regulate the liquidity in the banking system.
 
• It requires banks to maintain a certain percentage of their **net demand and time liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of **liquid assets **such as **cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• The SLR is determined by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and is currently set at **18.00% of NDTL.**
 
• Banks have to maintain this SLR on a **daily basis **and report it to the RBI every fortnight.
 
• SLR serves as a cushion against** unforeseen liquidity shocks** in the banking system.
 
• It also ensures that banks have **enough liquid assets t**o meet the demands of their depositors.
 
• Banks cannot** lend or invest **the funds that are kept in the SLR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal stability scheme** is a facility provided by the **RBI **to banks to borrow funds in case of temporary liquidity mismatches.
 
• **Open market operations** are the buying and selling of government securities by the **RBI** to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• **Legal deposit ratio** is not a commonly used term in banking.
